text:
elaine: Quick proposal — we should add a "score gating" concept to the reranker API + console. Idea: callers can set a min_score and a provenance tag (model/raw/normalized) and the gateway will either filter, fallback, or augment candidates before charging.

matt: Curious — is this primarily a client-side hint or a server-side enforcement?

elaine: Server-side enforcement. Two motivations: 1) reduce downstream work (UI / search) by filtering low quality candidates earlier, 2) enable predictable unit billing (we can count only returned candidates unless configured otherwise).

rafael: We need to be careful about what "score" means across models. Raw logits vs calibrated probs vs internal model rankers differ a lot. If we expose min_score, it must be tied to a normalization policy.

elaine: Agreed — propose three score namespaces: raw, softmax, normalized_percentile. Default is normalized_percentile (0-100) which is model-agnostic for gating. Raw is allowed but only with "model_affinity" set so routing knows what to expect.

sophie: From a console UX perspective, we'd want a single slider for the min_score (0-100) and a toggle for "enforce at gateway" vs "client-side hint". Also show a histogram of score distribution for the last 24h and a projected candidate drop-rate.

matt: For routing, we can use a per-model affinity score. If a request sets min_score=80 and model X historically can't reach that, the router should either 1) fall back to a stronger model, 2) return a partial result with a flag, or 3) return an explicit empty set. Need defaults.

elaine: Proposed default fallback policy: try model_affinity chain (preferred -> compatible -> fallback), if none can meet min_score use "best_effort" and add metadata: {"score_gating": "best_effort", "expected_drop_pct": "xx%"}.

rafael: Telemetry we need: score_distribution_{model}_{window}, gating_drop_pct, gating_chargeable_candidates, gating_latency_impact_ms. Also tag by route and by rollout (canary vs stable) so product can correlate quality regressions to rollouts.

sophie: For the console dashboard: small card with: slider, histogram, expected cost delta (tokens * candidates_retained), and a "preview on sample prompt" button that runs a dry-run and shows result. Dry-run should not decrement quotas.

elaine: API sketch (rough):

```json
POST /v1/rerank
Body: {
  "query": "...",
  "candidates": [...],
  "score_gating": {
    "namespace": "normalized_percentile",
    "min_score": 75,
    "fallback_policy": "model_affinity|best_effort|return_empty",
    "charge_on_filtered": false
  }
}
```

matt: Nice. On billing: "charge_on_filtered": false is the confusing bit for customers — they may expect to be charged per candidate the model evaluated, not per returned. We need explicit policy and console tooltips. Recommend default true (charge for evaluated) and an enterprise opt-out for "charge only returned" since it complicates capacity accounting.

elaine: Makes sense. Default charge_on_filtered = true. We'll add a clear note in Console: "If you enable charge_on_filtered=false, model will only bill for candidates returned; this may increase latency and cause fallback model usage."

rafael: For rollout UX: when we change normalization or introduce a new model_affinity chain, console should create a "compatibility simulation" run for a configurable sample set and show possible client-visible differences and cost delta. Suggest a canary toggle that runs gating in simulation for 24-72h and records metrics without enforcing.

sophie: UX mocks: https://redwood.internal/protos/score-gating-mock.png (placeholder). Card has: current setting, preview, last_simulation_summary, and a link to open an eval set.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: rerank-gating-service v0.3.1 -> canary

elaine: One more operational note — we should export a metric "gating_policy_mismatch_count" when client requests a namespace we don't recognize; increment and return HTTP 400 with a helpful message listing supported namespaces.

matt: Also add a per-route quota meter: gating_effective_units where effective_units = candidates_retained * unit_multiplier(model,namespace). We'll surface this in per-route dashboards so teams can set alerts for unexpected spikes.

rafael: Can we avoid adding too many new counters? Recommend a composite metric: gating.{model}.{route}.{namespace}.{stat} where stat in [drop_pct, retained_count, evaluated_count]. That keeps naming consistent with other metrics.

elaine: Good. I'll draft the API PR + console mock and a short rollout plan: default off, enable simulation for 1 week, then opt-in in console per route, later enterprise feature toggle for charge_on_filtered=false.

sophie: Thanks — if you post the mock I'll add it to the UX board. :thumbsup:

elaine: Posting PR in a bit — marking this thread actioned.

console-bot: action created: "score-gating: draft API + console mock" assigned to elaine

rafael: One follow-up: we should document expected failure modes (e.g., normalization drift after fine-tuning) and include recommended monitoring thresholds. I'll append a short doc to the PR.

elaine: Perfect.
